meta.what: Two channels of laundered Russian oil missing from the model (roadmap round 6, C2): (1) fuel from Brunei's Hengyi refinery (Pulau Muara Besar), which runs Russian crude, by buyer; (2) Russian oil products relabelled in Turkish ports without refineries (Ceyhan, Marmara Ereglisi, Mersin; Dortyol/Hatay terminals inside the Ceyhan-Iskenderun figure) and re-exported to the EU, by buyer. Plus the matching amounts to take off Brunei and Turkiye.
meta.units: EUR bn, nominal, low/central/high; 2026 = January-August, not annualised. USD converted with ECB yearly averages: 2019 1.120, 2020 1.142, 2021 1.183, 2022 1.053, 2023 1.081, 2024 1.082, 2025 1.13, 2026 1.16.
meta.method: Brunei: Brunei-reported HS 2710 exports by partner averaged with partners' imports from Brunei (/1.05 CIF to FOB), UN Comtrade 2019-2025; 2026 Jan-Aug from partners' monthly imports (AUS, MYS, SGP Jan-Mar extrapolated, JPN, PHL; others = 2025 x 8/12 x 1.3). x Russian share of Hengyi crude (CREA Sep 2026: 5% 2022, 37% 2025, 72% Jan-Jul 2026; CREA Feb 2025/2026 and KSE/Kpler for 2024-26; Brunei customs and CREA tracker for 2020-2023) = Russian-derived fuel value; x CRUDE_CONTENT 0.42/0.50/0.60 = Russian crude value, the same ratio the builder uses. Turkish ports: value of EU imports from the three ports (CREA/CSD May 2024: EUR 3.1 bn Feb 2023-Feb 2024; CREA Feb 2026: EUR 3.3 bn Feb 2025-Jan 2026, Greece 2.54, Cyprus 0.289, Bulgaria 0.179, Malta 0.104, Spain 0.092), 2024 interpolated, 2026 from Greek Comext pace; x Russian share of port supply (82-86%) x Russian sale price / EU purchase price (0.9) = money Russia received (0.756 per euro; 0.52-0.90). This is Russian product, not refined from Russian crude, so it is valued at the full Russian product value, not CRUDE_CONTENT. Split by member from CREA (2025) and Comext origin data (Greek imports labelled Iraq, Turkmenistan, Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan). Greece resells 50% (energy2 hub_resale) to its customers (hub_exports_2024). Overlap with laundered_eu.json removed (Turkish-labelled part; Cyprus 'not specified' part).
meta.builder: Per buyer: add `add_total_eur_bn` to the laundered-oil (laund) values after apply_laundered_eu(). For AUS use `replacement_for_laundered_eu_non_eu_AUS.new_total` instead of laundered_eu non_eu AUS (add_total is the difference). For hubs (SGP, MYS, NLD) better: put the Brunei fuel value into the starting values of reassign_laundered_oil() so the hub pass-on applies. Pre-war: add `brunei.prewar_base_2018_2021_fuel_value` to LAUNDERED_PREWAR base (product stage) per buyer; the Turkish-port channel has a zero pre-war base. Turkiye: subtract `subtract_reexported_russian_products_eur_bn` from its payments to Russia (it equals the buyers' gross amount, incl. the part already in laundered_eu). Brunei: take off `refiner.deduct_exported_crude_value_eur_bn` (equals what the buyers are charged); because Brunei customs under-record Russian crude (cargoes labelled Malaysia after ship-to-ship transfers), first replace Brunei's crude line from Russia by `true_russian_crude_intake_eur_bn` (option B), or floor the result at zero (option A).

overlaps: Brunei: not in energy.json laundered_oil (refiners IN, TR, CN, AE) nor round4a laundered_prewar, so new for every buyer except Australia: laundered_eu.json non_eu AUS 2025 (0.90) is built from CREA's Mar 2025-Feb 2026 figure that includes Hengyi at 60% Russian (about 0.49 of the 0.90) and AUS 2026 (0.35) from CREA monthly tracking that includes some Hengyi cargoes (about 0.14); the AUS replacement series removes these. Brunei's own payments (trade_full customs) include its recorded Russian crude; the refiner deduction takes off exactly what the buyers are charged. Turkish ports: hub_buyers.json turkey_refining covers refinery output (STAR, Tupras) and is a different flow; its refiner deduction at Turkiye stays. The re-export block hub_buyers.json turkey_refining.reexport_of_russian_products (EUR 1.7-3.3 bn central) is the same flow and is replaced by this file (it was never added). The model's Turkey component for non-EU buyers (energy.json, national Russian share on all Turkish exports) partly covers non-EU re-exports; not changed here. laundered_eu.json: its Turkish-origin imports (TR share x k) contain the port cargoes declared as Turkish (assumed 20% for Greece, 40% for other members), and its Cyprus value (40% of 'not specified' imports) is the same cargoes; both are subtracted (`already_in_laundered_eu_eur_bn`, total about EUR 1.0 bn 2022-2026). Turkiye's subtraction is the gross amount, so the earlier double count (laundered_eu buyers + Turkiye's own payments) disappears too. Direct EU imports of Russian products in 2022 to Feb 2023 are in to_rus of the EU members and not here. Shadow-fleet and shipping files are about freight, not fuel value: no overlap.
notes: Educated guesses: 2024 Turkish-port value (interpolated), 2026 Turkish-port value (Greek Comext pace, wide range), the money-to-Russia factor, the member split outside 2025, the Turkish-labelled share used for the overlap, Brunei 2026 exports to destinations other than Australia, Hengyi's 2020-2021 Russian share (customs 25% vs CREA tracker 8% in 2021) and 2026 crude import value. Ukraine appears as a customer of Greek resale (hub_exports_2024): the builder may drop it if Ukraine is not scored. Gibraltar receives Greek resale as bunker fuel; the existing Gibraltar margin rule applies. Brunei crude also feeds Hengyi's paraxylene and benzene (sold mostly to China), which is not fuel and is not counted at any buyer; it stays with Brunei under option B. Non-EU exports from the three Turkish ports (about EUR 1-1.5 bn a year, buyers unknown) are not quantified per buyer.
